_what: The error count this branch is allowed to carry. tools/validate_cards.py reports 613 errors today; making that BLOCKING would paint every branch red permanently, and a permanently red CI is how this repo learned to ignore CI. So the gate is a RATCHET instead: the backlog may shrink, never grow. The ratchet reads its pass mark from the BASE branch, never from the branch it is judging, and refuses to compare a run that saw less than this one did.
_how_to_update: When the count goes DOWN, run `python3 tools/validate_cards.py --quiet --json /tmp/r.json` and commit the new number here in the same PR that lowered it. Never raise it to make a red build green — that is the grandfathering this validator exists to refuse.
_why: kredme-data is PUBLIC and KredMe-main is PRIVATE, so CI here can never check the app out. This baseline is therefore measured the way CI measures it: against the vendored tools/app_mirror/ category list. With a real app checkout the count is the same 610 — the mirror is current — but the run is DEGRADED either way and says so.
_why_this_number_rose: 554 -> 574. The ONLY kind of rise this file accepts: a NEW CHECK made an existing defect visible, in the same PR that added the check. L6.RULE_FIRES_WIDER_THAN_ITS_EVIDENCE contributes 22 findings covering 60 reward rules whose own wording restricts the rate to a platform, payment rail, transaction size, membership or date that no field the engine reads can hold — so the app fires them across a whole category. Not one of those rules changed in this PR; they were all already live and already wrong. Nothing is grandfathered: every finding prints, lands in the JSON and the HTML, and drops its card out of the clean column. The four PhonePe cards and Axis Cashback fixed in PR #69 are deliberately ABSENT from the list — the check clearing the cards it was written for is the evidence that it measures the right thing. This number must go DOWN from here; the next PR to touch it should be one that fixes cards on the list, not one that raises it.
